literal: name-my. This is a direct and perfectly idiomatic construction.
usage: This is the standard and most common way to introduce yourself in Moroccan Darija, used in both formal and informal situations. It is universally understood across all regions of Morocco and is appropriate for speaking to anyone regardless of age or status.

variants.label: your name (singular)
variants.note: Used when addressing one person directly, regardless of gender.

variants.label: his name
variants.note: Used when stating or asking the name of a male third party.

variants.label: her name
variants.note: Used when stating or asking the name of a female third party.

variants.label: they call me
variants.note: Used to introduce a nickname or the name you prefer to go by.

examples.arabic: سْمِيتِي سَارَة، وْ نْتَا شْنُو سْمِيتَك؟
examples.transliteration: smiti sarah, w nta shno smitk?
examples.english: My name is Sarah, and you, what is your name?
I am American and my name is John.
